clue.text: Tolkien hole-builder in a fireside piece

parts.note: a hob is a shelf beside a fireplace, so it stands for the fireside
a bit is a small piece of something

explanation.surface: A Tolkien creature appears as an ornament on a fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the famous opening line about a creature living in a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's halflings famously live in burrows dug into hillsides.

clue.text: One raises the issue at mealtimes

definitions.text: One raises the issue at mealtimes

parts.words: One raises the issue at mealtimes
parts.note: issue means offspring: a piece of furniture that lifts a small child up to the table to eat

explanation.definitionFit: A tall chair with a tray in which a toddler sits to be fed.

clue.text: Sideshow touts who need shinguards?

explanation.definitionFit: Fairground criers drum up custom loudly; those who bark their shins (scrape them) would want protective pads.

clue.text: Fashionable apartment fitted, suitable for gazumping?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a flat is an apartment
fitted for something means able to do it

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb for a trendy furnished flat ripe for a sneaky higher bid.
explanation.walkthrough: Gazumping, in British property sales, is a seller accepting a higher offer after agreeing a price; so something whose price can be blown up.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being blown up or increased, as prices are when buyers outbid one another.

clue.text: Container for basic soups recipe taken from town in Greater Manchester

indicators.note: taken from says one letter is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England
R, from the Latin recipe, heads prescriptions and stands for recipe

explanation.surface: A cookery note explaining where a soup pan's recipe came from.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the abbreviation for recipe (take) used on prescriptions; removing it from STOCKPORT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock, the base of many soups, is simmered in this large cooking vessel.

clue.text: Stand for serving soldiers

parts.note: soldiers are strips of bread for dipping in a boiled egg, and stand means a holder for serving them at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain soldiers are narrow fingers of buttered bread, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack holding slices of grilled bread upright on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Old Egyptian reportedly collared?

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: copped is slang for collared, caught or arrested

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian, so the story goes, was arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt is a native Egyptian Christian, descendant of the ancient Egyptians.

clue.text: Left one firm to build a colonnade

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral one
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business hires one company to put up a row of columns.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch whose roof is supported by a row of columns.

clue.text: Decimal point perfect, possibly

parts.note: decimal refers to the number ten
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A decimal point placed precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' looks like an adjective but is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is one example of a grammatical form of a verb showing time.

clue.text: Utter loss from plunder in old Chester

indicators.note: loss from says the second word is removed from the first

parts.note: to devastate is to lay waste or plunder
to state is to utter or declare

explanation.surface: A complete loss caused by looting in historic Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (total) but is the verb, STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deva was the Roman name for the fortress town that became Chester.

clue.text: Animal with the most superior brain

definitions.text: Animal with the most superior brain

parts.words: Animal with the most superior brain
parts.note: superior is read literally as highest up: the creature whose brain sits furthest above the ground, thanks to its long neck

explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked African mammal is the tallest animal, so its head is the highest of all.

clue.text: Endlessly striving for a pain-reliever

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for striving for is dropped

parts.note: aspiring means striving for or aiming at

explanation.surface: Someone working without end in pursuit of relief from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A common analgesic tablet taken for headaches and other aches.

clue.text: Chance a lot cooking fish thought to have gone off?

definitions.text: fish thought to have gone off?

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are being worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a big risk by cooking a fish that may have spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' looks like spoiled food but means gone extinct: this fish was believed extinct until one was caught in 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: A primitive lobe-finned fish known only from fossils until a living specimen turned up off South Africa.

clue.text: Excellent brandy!

explanation.definitionFit: Fine means of high quality, and fine is also a name for a French brandy (as in fine champagne).

clue.text: Birth and death of a backbiter

explanation.definitionFit: Extraction means descent or lineage; a backbiter is jokingly a back tooth, whose end comes when the dentist pulls it.

clue.text: Appease appetite for fresh sausage

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Satisfying hunger with a newly made sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to satisfy or relieve a craving, such as hunger.

clue.text: Basic habitat on a lake

parts.note: one's element is one's natural environment or habitat
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A simple home beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or primary.

clue.text: Eight down, say, and worried

explanation.definitionFit: The entry at 8 down is TENSE, which is one example of nervous, and being on edge means being worried.

clue.text: Judge in Sark orders lass hence

indicators.note: orders means puts the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Channel Island magistrate sends a girl away.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island whose seneschal presides over its court.
explanation.definitionFit: The seneschal of Sark is the island's chief judicial officer.

clue.text: Rook's early openings beat check

indicators.note: openings asks for the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: a pulse is a regular beat, as of the heart

explanation.surface: A chess note: an early rook move answers a check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'check' look like a chess term; here it is a verb meaning to drive back.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an attack is to hold it back or repel it.

clue.text: Combination of colours just right on sea bird?

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, places the first piece above the bird

parts.note: pat means exactly right or apt
a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: The plumage on a sea bird having exactly the right colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A design or arrangement of shades, such as a repeated motif.

clue.text: Nail-hardener used by a tinker at Inch

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker in a Scottish place called Inch uses something to harden nails.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous protein makes up fingernails, hair and horn, giving them their toughness.

clue.text: Pot's rim damaged by plant's response to stimulus

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are broken and put back differently

explanation.surface: A plant pot's edge is harmed by the plant growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropism is growth turned towards or away from a stimulus such as light.

clue.text: Woman makes impression on field, opening Hickstead

parts.note: a rut is a groove or track worn into the ground

indicators.note: opening asks for the first letter of the place name

explanation.surface: A rider's horse leaves marks in the ground at the start of the Hickstead show.
explanation.walkthrough: Hickstead is an English showjumping venue in Sussex, which suits the field picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's name, also borne by a woman in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Old cold rhubarb

explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is an old word for catarrh or a running cold, and Rheum is the botanical genus of rhubarb.

clue.text: US comedian, as it turns out, is lying

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: An American comic's act is revealed to be dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacious describes someone untruthful, given to telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Dead astern is simple

parts.note: aft means at or towards the stern

explanation.surface: A naval term for directly behind is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft means silly or foolish, which is one sense of simple.

clue.text: Man, a little lower?

parts.note: the Isle of Man has a small islet off its southern tip, and on a body a lower leg part sits below the knee

explanation.walkthrough: The Calf of Man is a little island just south of the Isle of Man, which is in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow is small, the islet beside Man is small, and the back of the lower leg is low.

clue.text: Courtly English ambassador cut down when carrying letter

indicators.note: carrying means the shortened envoy holds the letter inside it
cut down says the word for an envoy loses its final letter

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially a papal one
en, N, is the name of a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An English diplomat is cut short while holding a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims LEGATE to LEGAT, and 'carrying' puts N inside it to give LEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and refined in manner, as people at a royal court are expected to be.

clue.text: Rather light melody in The Trout, say?

indicators.note: in places the tune inside the creature

parts.note: a trout is an example of a fish
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A tune within Schubert's Trout Quintet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trout is a famous Schubert work, so the musical picture hides the plain creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means pale or blond, so somewhat fair is moderately pale in colour.

clue.text: Chap, though elderly, is performing several functions at once

parts.note: a chap is a man
if can mean even though, as in a pleasant if dull day
elderly means old

explanation.surface: An aged man still multitasking.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means having many different forms or uses at the same time.

clue.text: Beast with thin plate on its back

indicators.note: on its back says the word for a thin plate is turned over and read the other way

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A creature with a thin plate fixed to its back, like armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature, especially a non-human one.
